item.description:
Rein 0.9.10

  • Email-code gate: Check just works. Rein now reads everything it needs from the page's own sign-in redirect — no Cloudflare API, nothing to paste. The setup sheet shows one clear status line; the Cloudflare steps fold away until you need them.
  • Your iPhone stays trusted after a browser session. Allowing a second device (a laptop browser) no longer replaces the phone's saved pairing — every device you've allowed stays allowed.
  • Rein Remote can show you the browser address. The Mac now publishes the web remote's address to the phone; Rein Remote 0.2.5 shows it (with the Mac's name and the pairing code) in the Controls drawer.
  • Web remote fills the window instead of showing the Mac's screen small in a corner.

Rein 0.9.8

Web remote: an email code in front, no Allow prompt behind.

  • Require email code. Remote → Web remote → *Require email code…* puts a Cloudflare Access

one-time email code in front of the browser page, on your own free Cloudflare account. Rein sets

it up through the API with the token it already holds for the relay; if that token can't manage

Access, Rein shows the three dashboard steps and then picks up the result itself — nothing to paste.

  • Browsers that sign in are approved automatically. The page sends the Access sign-in it arrived

with; the Mac verifies it offline against your team's published keys and — only if it names your

email and this exact app — trusts the browser for the session. The code you typed *is* the

approval. Anything unverifiable still gets the ordinary Allow prompt, and a browser session never

replaces your phone's saved pairing.

Also carries 0.9.7's fan work: the fan curve now reads the SoC die (the old input was a constant),

a new default matched to Apple's measured behaviour, curve presets, and smoother dynamics.

Rein 0.9.6

  • Virtual Devices now do what the screen says. Activate a device and its sources really feed

it: an app source is copied into the device (the app keeps playing where it was), a microphone

source is passed through into it, and each monitor plays the device's mix on the output you

chose, at the volumes you set — all scaled by the device's master. The L/R meters on the device

card and the meter on every source are live. The status chip on the card tells you exactly what

is running ("Live · 2 sources · 1 monitor") or what's missing ("Publish to system to go live").

  • A real channel map. Publish a device with 4 or more channels and each source picks which

channel pair it lands on — a small patch bay for multi-track recording into one device.

  • Fixed: routing an app to a device that has inputs. Sending an app to a USB interface (or a

Rein device) could copy the interface's *input* back out instead of the app. Rein now finds the

right stream.

  • Extra brightness backs off when the Mac runs hot. Above 90 °C on the hottest sensor the XDR

boost pauses (the slider drops to hardware max and an amber note explains); it comes back below

80 °C and restores where you had it.

  • Housekeeping: "Show in Activity" in Virtual Devices is a working link; the templates now

pre-wire the current mic / output; a placeholder view that no screen used is gone.
